CaptureContinuityEvidence.description: Successful native input continuity bound to one exact, privately saved WAV.
CaptureContinuityEvidence.title: CaptureContinuityEvidence

CatalogEvent.description:
The catalog the service pinned for this process: the exact suite and its reference.

A plain correlated reply to ``CatalogCommand``, never a state snapshot. The app builds its
prompts and Library from ``catalog`` and names ``reference`` when it opens a context.
Validation fails (``ValidationError``) unless ``catalog`` hashes to
``reference.catalog_sha256`` and repeats its suite id and purpose; the recording service
reports such a reply as the terminal ``RECORDING.INVALID_MESSAGE``.
CatalogEvent.title: CatalogEvent

CatalogReference.description:
A published catalog version by id, version, exact suite digest and snapshot digest.

``catalog_sha256`` is the canonical digest of the suite alone (the digest every take
and coverage projection keys on); ``snapshot_sha256`` is the sha256 of the exact
snapshot file bytes, so the alias half of the file is pinned too. ``suite_id`` and
``purpose`` repeat what the snapshot's suite declares so contract-level checks (purpose
against the capture gate) need no file read; the store verifies all of them against the
snapshot whenever a reference is materialized.
CatalogReference.title: CatalogReference

FineTuneEvent.description: A fine-tune job's run record changed (written, finished or failed).
FineTuneEvent.title: FineTuneEvent

FineTuneProgressEvent.description:
Where one fine-tune job stands; sent as it moves and repeated in status replies.

``stage`` is the step a running job is in. Training progress (``epoch`` of ``epochs``,
``update``, ``loss``, ``eta_seconds`` remaining) is parsed from the trainer's log.
``error`` is present exactly when the job failed; a cancelled job carries none.
FineTuneProgressEvent.title: FineTuneProgressEvent

FineTuneRunSummary.description:
One training run as the app sees it: ``finetune.FineTuneRun`` without absolute paths.

Paths are relative to the asset root, and every sample lies under ``run_root``. Only a
finished run has samples (``finetuned`` from the trained checkpoint, ``base`` from the
pretrained weights, for comparison). ``reference_prompt_ids`` are the run's
reference-candidate prompts that have a clip in its dataset, in catalog order: the
reference choices Speak offers for this run (empty: Speak uses the run's first clip).
FineTuneRunSummary.title: FineTuneRunSummary

FineTuneStatusEvent.description:
Reply to ``fine-tune-status``: the runtime, the active job and the finished runs.

``active`` is always reported. ``finished_runs`` are the newest finished runs (at most
32, newest first: latest finish time, then greater run id) and ``latest_run`` is the
first of them. When they cannot be resolved (an unreadable or invalid ``run.json`` under
``derived/finetune``), both are absent and ``latest_run_error`` names why; a new job can
still be started.
FineTuneStatusEvent.title: FineTuneStatusEvent

PreparedCaptureGate.description: Previously verified corpus approval identity, invalidated when its evidence changes.
PreparedCaptureGate.title: PreparedCaptureGate

Prompt.description: One catalog entry. Optional v2 fields are omitted when absent so v1 bytes never change.
Prompt.title: Prompt

RecordingBuildIdentity.description: Exact executable, source-tree and environment identities; mutable tags are insufficient.
RecordingBuildIdentity.title: RecordingBuildIdentity

RecordingFileIdentity.description: Prepared authorization identity, including ctime to detect preserved-mtime changes.
RecordingFileIdentity.title: RecordingFileIdentity

RecordingFrameRange.description: Source-frame recipe, independent from eventual derivative rendering.
RecordingFrameRange.title: RecordingFrameRange

RecordingGroup.description:
One capture context: subject, catalog, device, host and corpus gate.

recording-group/v1 embeds the exact ``catalog`` (every group written before the corpus
store; readable forever, byte-identical). recording-group/v2 carries ``catalog_reference``
to a published corpus-store snapshot instead and embeds no catalog; its prompts are read
through ``corpus_store.resolve_group_catalog``. Containers (capture-reservation/v1,
recording-take/v1, recording-package-map/v1, responses) keep their own versions and nest
either form. Absent optional fields are omitted so v1 canonical bytes never change.
RecordingGroup.title: RecordingGroup

RecordingGroupSummary.description: Bounded context summary, never a repeated catalog or complete take list.
RecordingGroupSummary.title: RecordingGroupSummary

RecordingHistoryEntry.description: Small indexed projection; history pages neither transmit catalogs nor read WAVs.
RecordingHistoryEntry.title: RecordingHistoryEntry

RecordingPromptSummary.description: Bounded row projection; the client already owns exact catalog text.
RecordingPromptSummary.title: RecordingPromptSummary

RecordingRecoveryFinding.description: One observed result; pending results remain explicitly awaiting recheck.
RecordingRecoveryFinding.title: RecordingRecoveryFinding

RecordingRecoveryInventoryPage.description: Disposable inventory coverage, independent of canonical history completeness.
RecordingRecoveryInventoryPage.title: RecordingRecoveryInventoryPage

RecordingReviewSource.description: Authorization for one original; native playback verifies this exact descriptor/digest.
RecordingReviewSource.title: RecordingReviewSource

RecordingTransition.description: Reliable legal transport edge; repeated commands return the existing result.
RecordingTransition.title: RecordingTransition

ReviewActionEvent.description: Legacy actions bind an authorized source without inventing a native reservation.
ReviewActionEvent.title: ReviewActionEvent

SynthesisEvent.description:
Where one Speak request stands: the ``synthesize`` reply and its background events.

``model`` and ``text`` repeat the request. ``run_id`` (the fine-tuned run that spoke;
never for ``base``), ``reference_run_id`` and ``reference_prompt_id`` are known once the
worker has resolved the request, so a queued request names none. A finished request
names its clip: ``relative_path`` under ``derived/speech/<operation_id>/``, a private
24 kHz 16-bit mono WAV whose ``frames`` come from its header, ``seconds`` =
``frames / sample_rate_hz``, and ``sha256`` binding its bytes. ``error`` is present
exactly when the request failed; a cancelled request carries none.
SynthesisEvent.title: SynthesisEvent

VaultStatusEvent.description:
Reply to ``vault-status``, and the background update when the vault's state changes.

``state`` is what the app shows: ``off`` (this library is bound to no vault),
``up-to-date`` (the vault holds this library's files), ``waiting`` (files are waiting to
be copied, or an owner held its files back), ``copying`` (a pass is running),
``unreachable`` (the vault has answered with a retryable failure since
``unreachable_since``) or ``failed`` (a refusal that stops copying until the app is
relaunched; the binding is read once, when the service starts, so rebinding takes effect
only at the next launch, which is what ``voice-lab vault bind`` tells the user).
``waiting_files`` counts files no generation holds yet. ``generation`` is the newest
generation this service pushed (0 when it has pushed none) and ``last_pushed_at`` when it
did. ``code`` is the storage refusal behind an unreachable or failed vault, and
``message`` says what is wrong in the app's words.
VaultStatusEvent.title: VaultStatusEvent

WaveformCacheEvent.description: Derived-cache status never changes the successful raw capture decision or transport.
WaveformCacheEvent.title: WaveformCacheEvent
